Q: -rpath-link=dir not able to locate the shared library A:

When linking libraries (shared objects, or executables), the linker will use the following directories: (See man ld, or https://linux.die.net/man/1/ld - section about '-rpath-link'):

  1. Any directories specified with -L command line.

  2. Any directories specified by -rpath-link options.

  3. Any directories specified by -rpath options.

  4. if the -rpath and -rpath-link options were not used, directories included in the environment variable "LD_RUN_PATH".

  5. Directories included in the environment variable "LD_LIBRARY_PATH".

  6. The directories in "DT_RUNPATH" or "DT_RPATH" of a shared library are searched for shared libraries needed by it. The "DT_RPATH" entries are ignored if "DT_RUNPATH" entries exist.

  7. The default directories, normally /lib and /usr/lib.

  8. For a native linker on an ELF system, if the file /etc/ld.so.conf exists, the list of directories found in that file.

In this case:

  • libd.so is using rpath-link, which mean that he does not "remember" the directory ../a (It's not stored in the shared-object DT_RUNPATH).

  • When linking the main program, the effective search path for liba.so includes only d (from the -L), and b (from the -rpath-link).

  • As indicated by rule 6 above - even if the libd.so link was modified to use -rpath - it will NOT change the search path for building the main program. The '../a' directory will only be used to search for shared objects DIRECTLY needed by libd.so, and will not help resolve the reference from libb.so to liba.so.

Bottom line - you have to provide search path for "../a", when linking to libb.so, by

  • Providing -rpath/-rpath-link to "a" when linking the main program, OR

  • Providing -rpath to "a", when building libb.so

As an alternatives, if using LD_LIBRARY_PATH is an option, following rule #5 will simplify the build script:

  • LD_LIBRARY_PATH is set to ../a, ../b, ../d
  • All link commands will NOT need -rpath, -rpath-link, and -L

Q: How to see stashes in VS Code? A:

After installing Gitlens:

  • Navigate to Source Control from the left panel:

  • Expand the GITLENS accordian.

  • If you already have authorized you will see commits panel by default, if not authorized you will see a button which to link gitlens with you current source control.

  • After doing above step you will be able to see commits panel by default.

  • Switch right to the stashes panel.

    Additionally you can click on the three dots and select "Detach Stash View" to have different section of stashes.

Q: How to consume messages routed from rabbitmq mqtt plugin through rabbitmq streams A:

Not using rstream, but amqp works fine:

import pika, sys, os

def main():
    connection = pika.BlockingConnection(pika.ConnectionParameters(host='localhost'))
    channel = connection.channel()

    # Stream queues require an explicit prefetch; broker rejects consumers without it.
    channel.basic_qos(prefetch_count=100)

    def callback(ch, method, properties, body):
        print(f" [x] Received {body}")
        
        ch.basic_ack(delivery_tag=method.delivery_tag)

    # Stream queues do not support auto-ack; ack explicitly in callback.
    channel.basic_consume(queue='mqtt_stream', on_message_callback=callback, auto_ack=False)

    print(' [*] Waiting for messages. To exit press CTRL+C')
    channel.start_consuming()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    try:
        main()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print('Interrupted')
        try:
            sys.exit(0)
        except SystemExit:
            os._exit(0)
